notes: Hiding as the furniture so a grandma cannot catch you is prop-hunt hide-and-seek, squarely Party & Casual. The author put it in one small house for about six players, so I took interior-single from the shared catalogue rather than the genre's typical space-bounded: the whole map is a single enclosed building the player never leaves, which means no exterior to generate and no inside-outside transition, so it stays on P0 with no P3. Childhood Game keeps its options on that substituted shape, with obstacle-maze dropped because normal rooms and furniture are the opposite of a warren, and cover-los carrying the hideable furniture arrays. Without a user I decided the between-rounds gathering room lives inside the house rather than as a separate lobby map, which avoids splitting a deliberately small build; being able to morph into a prop and whether the grandma is an NPC or a player are gameplay roles rather than layout.
